key_points: Real activity is steady rather than accelerating: June payrolls +57k, unemployment down to 4.2%, initial claims low at 215k.
The Fed describes expansion as solid with strong productivity and capex (AI investment); the stale GDPNow of ~1.2% is the soft spot.
Consumer sentiment is depressed but rebounding (49.5 from 44.8). The 30% collapse in oil is a real-income tailwind for households and supports equities and tight credit.

With no growth shock in sight, yields at the top of their range have no strong directional push. Falling energy costs may eventually let the Fed ease, favoring a mildly lower front end and steeper 2s10s over 3 months.

Equity drift is positive on a soft-landing growth backdrop. HY spreads are already near tights, so there is little room for further compression, while VIX may mean-revert modestly higher off holiday-thin lows.

Headline CPI is running ~4.2% y/y (May +0.47% m/m) and core PCE ~3.4% y/y (+0.32% m/m): inflation is still well above target, which is why the Fed holds a hawkish lean and the 2y sits at the 97th percentile of its range.
WTI fell ~30% in a month and ~38% over 3 months; energy pass-through will pull headline CPI/PCE down sharply in the June–August prints, easing near-term hike risk priced into the front end.
The 10y breakeven at 2.23% (5th percentile) already reflects the oil collapse; sticky core and goods/tariff pressure limit further downside, so breakevens are roughly balanced.
Disinflation from energy favors a modest bull steepening: front-end yields are more exposed to a repricing of hike odds than the 10y, which carries a term premium.
Softer headline inflation supports risk assets and modestly weighs on the dollar; gold at the 3rd percentile could benefit from lower real-yield expectations.
Risks: core services and wage persistence (wages ~3.5% y/y, moderate) or a renewed oil spike from the Middle East would revive the hawkish case.
June payrolls +57k with unemployment down to 4.2% and claims at 215k: low-hire, low-fire labor market that is stable to slightly firmer, consistent with slow labor-force growth rather than fragility.
Firm labor data removes near-term pressure for Fed cuts but does not justify hikes; 2y at 4.14% vs funds midpoint ~3.63% already embeds a hawkish tilt, so modest downside skew for 2y over 3 months.
Jobs report already absorbed (10y +11bp on the week); next payroll prints in early August/September are the main labor catalysts, with risks two-sided given downside employment risks flagged by FOMC.
Stable employment and low claims support earnings and tight credit spreads, giving a mild positive tilt to equities and neutral-to-tight HY spreads.
Labor lens offers little edge on oil, gold, breakevens and the dollar; VIX near the low end of its range leaves slight upward mean-reversion risk over 3 months.
Fed on hold at 3.50-3.75%; June statement unanimous with hawkish 'will deliver price stability' language and easing bias apparently dropped.
2y at 4.14% sits ~50bp above effective funds rate, implying the market prices hikes; 97th percentile of 1y range.
WTI down 30% in a month and breakevens near 1y lows undercut the energy-driven inflation case behind hike pricing, favoring a drift lower in front-end yields over 3m.
Labor modest (payrolls +57k, UR 4.2%) gives no urgency to hike; a lower 2y with stickier term premium favors mild 2s10s steepening.
Near-term event risk: June minutes (Jul 8) likely hawkish, keeping 1w rate odds balanced.
Supportive financial conditions (NFCI -0.50) and a Fed not tightening keep equities with a mild upward drift; spreads and VIX near lows limit further compression.

Term premium is doing the work at the long end. Oil fell about 30% and 10y breakevens fell 15bp over the month, yet the 10y yield was unchanged. That points to a rising term premium, consistent with heavy coupon supply and large deficits.
The August quarterly refunding and steady coupon issuance fall inside the 1m-3m window. Supply pressure loads mainly on the long end, giving a mild bias toward higher 10y yields.
The 2y yield is near its 1y high on Fed hike pricing. With energy-driven inflation fading, the front end has more room to rally than the back end.
2s10s sits at the 4th percentile of its 1y range. Fiscal supply plus front-end relief favors steepening over 1m-3m.
The Fed's balance sheet is roughly flat to slightly declining, with reserve management purchases limited to bills. That gives no offset to duration supply.
Gold sits at the 3rd percentile of its 1y range. Fiscal-sustainability and debasement hedging gives modest upside, with weak support from this lens alone.
Equities, the dollar, oil and credit get only marginal fiscal signal, so those forecasts stay near base rates.
Financial conditions are loose: NFCI at -0.50, HY OAS 2.74% near 1y lows, VIX ~16 — supportive of risk assets near term.
Fed reserve management purchases keep reserves ample; money markets orderly (EFFR 1bp below IORB, minimal SRP/RRP use), no funding stress signal.
Balance sheet up ~$60bn y/y via bill purchases — mild liquidity tailwind, not a driver of duration yields.
Tight spreads and low VIX leave limited room for further compression; mean reversion risk grows over 3m, so edges fade with horizon.
Dollar near upper part of range with crowded long DX spec positioning; slight downside tilt as risk sentiment stays benign.
2y at 97th percentile with oil down 30% in a month; easing energy pressure plus Fed on hold tilts front end slightly lower and curve slightly steeper over 3m.
Dollar index spec net long at 97th percentile of its 52-week range, about 24% of open interest. That is a crowded long, so the risk is skewed to dollar weakness on any unwind.

E-mini S&P net position is the least short in a year (97th percentile). Equity momentum, a VIX of 15.8 and tight HY spreads support risk appetite, but the room left for short-covering fuel is limited.

Gold sits at the 3rd percentile of its 1y range after a 13% drop over 3 months, while spec length is only mid-range (43rd percentile) and was rebuilding this week (+12.7k). That looks washed out, a contrarian upside lean.

Treasury specs are still heavily net short in TY and TU but are covering, with 2y and 10y yields at the 94th-97th percentiles. That gives a mild contrarian lean toward lower yields and a steeper 2s10s curve from its 4th-percentile level.

HY OAS at 2.74 (13th percentile) and VIX at its 23rd percentile leave complacency asymmetric over 3 months. Fall seasonality and the September FOMC/SEP argue for a modestly higher VIX and wider spreads; near term the low-vol summer regime persists.
WTI positioning is neutral (45th percentile) after a 30% collapse, so positioning gives no edge. Breakevens at the 5th percentile give a slight mean-reversion lean higher.

Oil down ~30% in a month implies Middle East de-escalation; that removes the energy-driven inflation impulse abroad (notably Europe) that pushed AFE short-end yields and policy paths higher, which should pull global yields and US yields modestly lower over 1-3m.

Dollar rose 1.1% in a month despite risk-on and oil collapse, and DX speculative longs sit at the 97th percentile: crowded positioning plus fading safe-haven/terms-of-trade support argues for mild dollar weakness, as seen after the April cease-fire.

US 2y and 10y at 94th-97th percentile of their 1y ranges while foreign energy-related inflation pressure eases; Fed cut later in 2026 becomes more plausible, favoring a lower 2y and mild 2s10s re-steepening over 3m.
Weaker dollar and improved global risk appetite (AI optimism, foreign equity strength) support S&P 500 and offer some rebound potential for gold from 3rd-percentile levels.
Credit spreads and VIX are already near lows, limiting further compression; breakevens at the 5th percentile already reflect the oil drop, so roughly neutral there.
WTI has collapsed 30% in a month and 38% in three months from a ~$115 conflict peak to ~$70, consistent with the steeply backwardated curve the Desk flagged; the energy supply shock is unwinding.

Lower energy prices will feed through to headline CPI/PCE over coming months, undercutting the Fed's hawkish lean (a majority saw firming if inflation persisted); a 2y at 4.14, well above the 3.5-3.75 funds range, looks too high from an energy pass-through view, so front-end yields lean lower and 2s10s leans steeper.
Breakevens sit at the 5th percentile after the oil drop; further headline disinflation argues against a big rebound, though much is priced.

Oil itself is near fair after the crash, with spec length mid-range; re-escalation is a right-tail risk, offset by supply normalization, so probabilities are near neutral with a slight downside drift.
Gold is at the 3rd percentile of its 1y range after a ~13% drop, with specs adding length; that gives modest mean-reversion odds.

Cheaper energy is a tailwind for consumers (sentiment at 49.5) and corporate margins, which supports equities; HY spreads are already tight and energy issuers face slightly weaker cash flows, so spreads look neutral.
Middle East conflict appears to have de-escalated: WTI down ~30% in a month and ~38% in three months, gold near 1y lows, VIX down ~8 points over 3m — much of the peace dividend is already priced.

With risk premia compressed (HY spread 13th percentile, VIX 23rd percentile, breakevens 5th percentile), a geopolitical re-flare would hit asymmetrically: upside for oil, VIX, spreads and breakevens; that partly offsets continued normalization in the base case.

Fading energy shock lowers the inflation premium in front-end yields and weakens the case for Fed firming over 3m; long-dated term premium and fiscal/midterm dynamics argue for modest curve steepening from a 4th-percentile 2s10s.
Dollar safe-haven bid unwinds as conflict risk eases, and speculative DX longs are at the 97th percentile — mild downside bias for the broad dollar.

Tariff escalation risk (flagged by FOMC participants) and November midterm campaign noise into the Aug–Oct seasonally weak window modestly raise VIX odds at the 3m horizon, while equities retain a slight positive drift supported by earnings and AI capex.

thesis: The energy shock is unwinding. WTI is down about 30% in a month as the Middle East de-escalates, and that should pull headline inflation down over the summer. It also undercuts the hike pricing in a 2y yield of 4.14%, which sits about 50bp above the funds midpoint and at the 97th percentile of its range. So I lean toward a lower front end and a mild steepening from a 4th-percentile 2s10s, with the 10y held up by term premium and coupon supply. The labor market is steady (UR 4.2%, claims 215k), financial conditions are loose and AI capex continues, which supports a positive equity drift. HY spreads and VIX are already near their lows, so compression edges are small; I add a modest upward tilt for VIX and spreads at 3 months, covering the fall seasonality and re-escalation tail risk. Crowded spec dollar longs at the 97th percentile, plus a fading safe-haven bid, give a mild dollar-down lean. Gold at the 3rd percentile of its range, with specs adding length, gets a slight rebound lean. Oil and breakevens are roughly neutral after the large repricing. Near-term catalysts are the June minutes on July 8 (likely hawkish) and the July 29 FOMC, so 1-week edges stay small.
